 Emo wave swallows Bukit Jalil as MCR returns after nearly 19 years 
 Copy 
 Participants of Langgar Limit’s The Black Parade mini run. — Picture courtesy of Langgar Limit 
 Follow us on Instagram , subscribe to our Telegram channel and
 browser alerts 
 for the latest news you need to know. 
 By Arif Zikri 
 Thursday, 19 Nov 2026 7:20 PM MYT 
 KUALA LUMPUR, November 19 — Forget the blue wave — Bukit Jalil is drowning in an emo wave tonight as My Chemical Romance (MCR) kicks off the first night of The Black Parade 2026 in KL.The TM National Stadium in Bukit Jalil, serving as the tour’s penultimate venue, will host the rock band on November 19 and 20 with an estimated 120,000 fans attending both days.By early this morning, fans had already begun arriving, many clad in all-black outfits, some complete with MCR-themed face makeup and face paint.The hype for MCR has been building since the KL stop was announced last year and despite the postponement that moved the original April and May dates to November, fans are still going above and beyond to welcome MCR back to Malaysia after nearly 19 years.From an MCR-themed running event and an after party to trading customised fan freebies packs, Malaysians are ready for The Black Parade 2026.Twenty-six-year-old Akmal Hady is one of the founders of a Klang Valley-based running community collective called Langgar Limit, and the group recently organised an MCR-themed running event in Petaling Jaya."The idea for The Black Parade run came from one of our crew members, Muaz, back in July 2025 when tickets first went on sale."Basically, it’s a short run followed by a DJ after-party at Underturntable in PJ."We had a great turnout — around 80 people showed up,” Hady told Malay Mail.Hady added that many participants even came in their best emo-style sporting getups with some wearing band tees, chains, boots, makeup and eyeliner."Growing up, I listened to a lot of emo music, and MCR is easily one of the biggest icons of the subculture."After going to so many emo night gigs over the years, my team and I finally managed to organise one ourselves — and I’m honestly so proud of us,” Hady said.Meanwhile, 19-year-old Danny is one of the admins of the @fansprojectmcr_msia Instagram page and is currently on a mission to execute a fan project, a hybrid physical and digital fan light-up project in collaboration with a couple of local MCR fan pages, including @mcrxmalaysia and @MCRmymsia.The fan light-up project uses a mix of 20,000 red paper cutouts (printed with QR code instructions for the seating zones) and red-and-blue digital backgrounds that fans display on their phone screens at full brightness.They are asking participating fans to light up their phones or put up the cutouts during several songs throughout the concert."We started planning about two weeks after tickets dropped last year for the original April date. At first, around 80 people volunteered, but after the postponement, many members backed out quite late."Now we’re down to about 20 people, which made our original plan of printing 160,000 two-coloured papers impossible. Instead, we printed 20,000 red cutouts with QR instructions mainly for the seating zones, and switched to digital red and blue screens that fans can screenshot and display at full brightness,” Danny said.Danny was inspired to do the fan project after seeing MCR frontman Gerard Way’s reaction towards another light-up fan project at their previous concerts.He even made a new circle of online friends through Aling and Aiman over their shared love for MCR and, having never met face-to-face, the first night of the concert will mark their first real-life meetup."Two weeks after tickets went on sale, I searched to see if any Malaysians were doing something similar (fan project) and found a post by Aling that barely had any engagement."I reached out to her and the only person who commented on her post, Aiman, and we started a WhatsApp group to recruit more people."What’s crazy is that we’ve never met in real life — we’ve only ever talked online, and today will be our first time meeting,” Danny said, adding that the rest of the team consists of members from various age groups, ranging from Millennials to Gen Z.While most fans have been supportive, the team has faced gatekeeping from rock purists calling the project "too K-pop” and questioning whether they are "real rockers” — criticism the team takes in stride."The reception has been a bit of a mixed bag."Most people are backing us and sharing our posts, but there are definitely a few calling us ‘not real rockers’ or saying we’re acting like K-pop fans."Some people agree with that take, and honestly, we get it — you can’t please everyone,” he said.Bringing a heavy dose of early-2000s nostalgia to Bukit Jalil, 34-year-old small business owner Teh Fatimah Md Sidik — founder of custom printing brand Tehreka Studio — is handing out free retro cassette cover inserts and selling custom cassette fan packs across both nights of the concert.Inspired by fans sharing handmade crafts online and the lasting memories attached to physical music memorabilia, she wanted to create tangible keepsakes that would remind concertgoers of the night they finally saw MCR live after nearly 19 years."I started this project on Saturday, November 14, with around RM70 in capital for 200 freebie packs."I handled everything myself, from designing and mock-ups to printing, cutting, and packaging and it’s been completely worth it."Beyond introducing Tehreka Studio, I didn’t expect so many people to love the cassette concept because it brings back their teenage memories,” Teh told Malay Mail.There is no shortage of fans dressing up in their gothic and emo outfits in Bukit Jalil today, and one of them is 31-year-old Nur Fatin Shafiqa Mohd Norman from Batu Pahat, Johor.Shafiqa came clad in a black jacket, a handmade red songket tailored by her mother just a couple of days earlier, along with a black veil adorned with a black rose and gothic-themed makeup."We arrived in KL from Johor yesterday and we stayed at a hostel in KL and will be heading back to Batu Pahat tonight after the concert."We arrived at the stadium around 9am this morning because we were afraid that the parking would be full here.She also revealed that she had to wake up at around 4.45am this morning to start dressing up for the concert. It took her around two hours to finish her look today."I’ve been listening to MCR since my school days."Even though the postponement dampened the hype for a bit, the excitement definitely came rushing back as the new date got closer,” she said.Tonight marks the first night of MCR’s The Black Parade 2026 in KL.The concert opened with a performance by local rap-rock group Pop Shuvit at 7.15pm before MCR takes the stage at 8.30pm.
